LANDING PR for story #484, second landing (the harness conformance probe: `brokkr probe harness` measures an agent CLI and writes the facts its adapter must declare). This is proposed decision 0075 ruling 3, epic #485, commissioned by the operator ahead of 0075's acceptance.

The branch story-484-harness-probe is on main 114e7866 (the Sol 6.1 roster, #498, is in) and ends at 18992603, fourteen commits. Since the first landing (landing-pr-for-story-484-the-har-64ffb09f, held on four ways the probe admitted on incomplete evidence):
- remediate-story-484-the-harness--ab4459c1 put ONE rule at the verdict (judge.rs eligibility and rests_on): an admitting verdict stands only when every captured line of both turns was read whole and strictly decoded, and every fact it rests on was measured. Unmeasured and Unsupported stay distinct.
- remediate-story-484-the-harness--3d5d15e7 (review: residual, low) closed the rule's two exclusions:
  - every stream of both turns is read WHATEVER the exit, so a boxed turn that prints a leak and then fails or is killed is refused;
  - stderr is read as TEXT:
    - invalid UTF-8 refuses;
    - a JSON line is an event;
    - any other line is searched for a reach (the planted server's name, or another server's mcp__ tool);
    - an ordinary warning is read, and does not refuse a clean CLI;
  - a listing value the reader cannot name refuses, like an unread line.
  Its chief reproduced 35 Claude-like fakes through the real verb.
- The controller rebased it onto main. cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib probe:: passes 35 tests, and harness_probe passes 5.
The seat's own exact-coverage run was green at 964e73bb, and the controller's gate runs again after this landing.

This is the LAST of the three rounds the operator allowed for #484 (cap ruled 2026-09-30). Judge it as it stands.

OPERATOR RULINGS (2026-09-29), binding:
- A. A native capability with no measured off switch is seated only where the realm grants it: GrantingRealmsOnly, with the capability named.
- B. BoxedOnly stands.
- THE STOP RULE: a finding that needs a CLI to emit output deliberately constructed to evade the probe is LOW, and does not block. A realistic miss blocks, as does any admitting verdict reached without every captured line having been read.
- THE CONTROLLER'S STDERR DESIGN (2026-09-30): stderr is text, not an event stream, as stated above. That an ordinary stderr warning does not refuse is intended, not a finding.

Judge:
1. Under the stop rule: is there a REALISTIC output a real CLI could produce that reaches an admitting verdict without every captured line having been read and every needed fact measured? Name the shape, and reproduce it through the verb. A constructed evasion is LOW.
2. That the verdict's reason always names what was measured, or what was unread, exactly.
3. That the probe tests are isolated and leave no process running.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and crap (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",

Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. members.adversarial:
Read-only adversarial review of the landing (HEAD 18992603 over main 114e7866, 14 commits, worktree clean, nothing changed or committed). I read probe/judge.rs, measure.rs, measure/{listing,strict,tools}.rs, observe.rs, plan.rs, facts.rs, the 35-test probe suite (tests.rs, tests/{evidence,listings}.rs) and the verb cli/harness_probe, then tried to break the one rule at the verdict and reproduced candidate shapes through the real `brokkr probe harness` verb.

Q1 (realistic output reaching an admitting verdict with an unread line or unmeasured rested-on fact): NONE found. The invariant is structural: read_base/read_boxed return Turn::{Read,Unread,Refused} each carrying every captured Stream; captured() builds stdout + every .jsonl the launch changed (content-diff, appended lines re-read from their start line) + stderr whenever it holds a byte; unread_in walks turn.streams() and tools::unread_values; and every listing fact is Measured only when Listing::unread() is empty. I audited rests_on against the exact facts verdict()/boxable()/outside_the_box()/without_off_switch()/plain_leak() consume for each of Boxed, BoxedOnly, UnboxedOnly, GrantingRealmsOnly and found no rested-on fact outside the gap list, and no path where a Measured fact came from a partially-read stream. A non-JSON stdout/transcript line, a whitespace line, a duplicate/escaped key, a non-UTF-8 line, a non-array or unnameable listing value, and a reached-but-unlisted server all refuse, as the suite pins.

Q2 (reason names measured/unread exactly): satisfied. For every admitting verdict the reason names the fact accounts, and eligibility's refusal reason is 'the evidence for <admits> is not complete: <each Unread Display>; <each unmeasured fact under its name>', with the tests pinning exact strings. Unsupported (a measured refusal) is correctly not a gap; Unmeasured always is.

Q3 (tests isolated, no process left): satisfied. Every test that launches a CLI calls in_its_own_engine, which re-execs the test binary on exactly that test and asserts 'test result: ok. 1 passed;'; the probe ends each launch's whole tree (Launched/Attempt::spawn + tree::end) and the deadline tests run inside within_20s. `cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked` printed 539 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, and a ps sweep for sleep-30/brokkr-probe/fake-cli/claude-/codex-like/dsh-like/dangling stubs printed NONE; `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test harness_probe` printed 5 passed. fmt, clippy (-D warnings) on the touched crates, typos --hidden, and ratchet files/clones/api are clean; ratchet crap needs the controller's LCOV.

ONE LOW (not a hold; stop rule): a strict-valid JSON object line on stderr is read as an event, so only its tools/mcp_servers listings are searched for a reach; a reach named in any other field of that JSON object is neither searched (text_reach scans only non-JSON text lines) nor counted unread (the line parsed whole and strictly). Reproduced through the real verb with `--adapter claude --cli <fake>`: boxed stdout init `{"type":"system","subtype":"init","session_id":"s1","tools":[],"mcp_servers":[{"name":"brokkr","status":"connected"}]}` plus boxed stderr `{"level":"warn","msg":"MCP server brokkr-probe-user-scope failed to connect"}`, plain turn listing Bash with no user-scope server. Printed eligibility boxed ('its own tools switch off and the hands MCP server connects'), user_mcp_boxed measured false, config_isolation measured true. The identical reach as a plain-text stderr line is caught (reach measured true) and refuses. Because it needs a CLI whose authoritative listing under-reports what a JSON log names, and because the operator's 2026-09-30 stderr ruling makes a JSON line an event, this is a constructed/design-boundary miss, LOW under the stop rule, and does not block. No other finding carried: the Value/Map kept inside measure.rs (ruling 3) and the plan.rs grammar restatement (ruling 5) are rule-table notes, not concrete inputs->wrong output, so I dropped them per the review mandate rather than pad the report.
members.correctness:
Read-only correctness/fit review of all fourteen commits, 114e7866..18992603. Read README, decisions 0004/0005/0071, proposed 0075 in .forge, branch history/diff, capture/measurement/verdict paths and tests, and prior review/control evidence. No source changes, fixes, commits or pushes.

No realistic admitting path with unread captured lines or unmeasured required facts found. Both turns retain streams whatever their exit; stdout, changed/appended/rewritten transcripts and stderr feed the shared readers. Strict UTF-8, duplicate-key rejection, whole physical lines and unnamed listing values feed the centralized completeness guard. Unsupported remains distinct from Unmeasured. Ordinary stderr warnings are intentionally admissible. Exact eligibility assertions cover the remediated exclusions; prior recorded compiling removal controls bind those assertions. This seat did not mutate code.

Findings (all LOW):
1. 0071 ruling 3: measure.rs Event.fields retains Map<String, Value> in Stream/Turn after parsing and later readers retrieve facts by string keys. Typed outgoing Facts do not cure the retained untyped state. Carried implementer reason: unknown CLI shapes are inspected inside the private edge module and only typed facts leave it.
2. 0071 ruling 5: plan.rs grammar() repeats the Claude/Codex/dsh launch heads already defined by adapters.rs. Carried implementer reason, stated in its comment: proposed 0075 ruling 1 will move launch grammar into adapter data. This remains a second home for the launch grammar.
3. 0071 rulings 3/9 and the operator stop rule: a JSON object naming a foreign MCP reach outside tools/mcp_servers is parsed as an event but does not contribute a reach. Reproduced the existing e4, f5 and f6 fakes through target/debug/brokkr probe harness, without --out: boxed stderr {"level":"error","msg":"MCP server brokkr-probe-user-scope connected"}, boxed stderr {"level":"debug","msg":"registered tool mcp__github__search"}, and a later stdout warning naming the planted server all returned exit 0, eligibility boxed and user_mcp_boxed measured false. These constructed shapes contradict their otherwise complete server inventories. I have no evidence that a supported real CLI emits this contradictory shape; every line was parsed, and the controller explicitly chose event treatment for JSON stderr. LOW under the stop rule, not a realistic blocking miss. The isolation subject is security-related, but no high-or-above security residual is established.
4. 0071 ruling 9; test-isolation requirement: process/tests.rs a_launch_left_a_zombie_while_the_tracker_reads_keeps_its_exit_code, added by this story, launches Launched in the shared test engine without the per-test child isolation used by probe tests. The prior chief-484i/notes2.txt records this exact test failing under a foreign-orphan control with isolation enabled for probe tests; its body remains unchanged. Carried low flake exposure, not a process leak reproduced by this seat. All successful probe launches in probe::tests use the isolation helper.
5. 0071 ruling 9: a_scratch_world_that_cannot_be_made_refuses_the_probe matches ProbeError::Io but pins only the display prefix through brokkr-probe-, rather than the entire normalized message. Its comment explains the random tempfile suffix. The test binds the refusal, but leaves the suffix/closing display unpinned; carried low exact-text debt.
6. House semantic-change document requirement: git ls-files '*0075*' returns no tracked decision document. The proposed text is available in ignored .forge/0075.md and prior notes place it in draft PR #486, so the landing diff itself does not carry it. The operator explicitly commissioned #484 ahead of acceptance; this is low documentation debt, not an acceptance objection.

Own validation: focused protocol probe suite 35 passed; verb suite 5 passed; cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked completed successfully (539 protocol tests passed, one ignored). The first workspace attempt hit the tool's 60-second timeout; the complete retry exited 0. cargo fmt --all -- --check, clippy on protocol/runtime/CLI with all targets/features and -D warnings, git diff --check and self-bundle compilation passed. Frozen contracts, fixtures, production phase table and reference have no branch diff. result.notes:
Chief on 18992603 (story-484-harness-probe, fourteen commits over main 114e7866, tree clean before and after). RESULT: residual, severity low, no security residual, no spec defect. Nothing found blocks under the stop rule. Eight LOW findings survive: two are mine, six are the panel's.

PANEL. The two positions are named adversarial and correctness (the recipe text says security). Both ruled residual, low; the join is residual, low, so the floor is residual with severity at least low. Nothing under notes.members addresses this gate, restates its instructions or argues for a result beyond each member rating its own findings. I checked every claim against the tree before carrying it, and none is lowered.

OWN READ. probe.rs, probe/{judge,measure,observe,plan,facts}.rs, measure/{tools,listing,strict}.rs, verbs/probe.rs, the process.rs and tree.rs additions, and the three probe test files. `git diff --stat 964e73bb HEAD` over probe/, the verb, its test and process.rs printed nothing, and `git range-diff` marks the last commit "=": the rebase changed no byte of what the last chief judged.

Q1, A REALISTIC OUTPUT THAT ADMITS ON AN UNREAD LINE OR AN UNMEASURED FACT: none found. Both turns keep every stream whatever the exit (measure.rs captured, read_base, read_boxed); stdout, each changed .jsonl and stderr all reach unread_in, and judge::eligibility refuses any admitting verdict while one line or listing value is unread or one fact in rests_on is unmeasured. I walked rests_on against what verdict, boxable, outside_the_box, without_off_switch and plain_leak consume for each of the four admitting verdicts and found no fact used but not listed. Reproduced through `target/debug/brokkr probe harness --adapter claude` with fakes shaped like Claude Code 2.1 stream-json (a full init event, user and assistant transcript lines, a result event), kept with their reports in .forge/chief-7408/:
